passage:
On Friday afternoon, Mina and Ravi are making a simple meal for six people at their community center. They choose a vegetable dish and a small loaf of bread. Everyone has different preferences, so Mina writes a note before they begin. One guest does not eat cheese, and another prefers food without much salt. The two cooks decide to put cheese on the table separately so that each person can choose.

Ravi checks each ingredient against their list. They have one onion, a little garlic, two carrots, three potatoes, a tomato, and a can of beans. Mina picks up a bean that has fallen from the can and puts it in the food-waste container. They also have flour, a little sugar, oil, black pepper, and a mild spice. They do not need to buy anything else. Ravi has already washed the vegetables, so Mina begins to peel the potato and chop the onion. Ravi will slice the carrot and tomato for the pan.

First they mix flour with water and a small amount of oil for the bread. They shape it and put it in the oven. Next, Ravi puts a little oil in a pan and begins to fry the onion and garlic. Mina adds the carrot and tomato. She asks Ravi to stir the vegetables while she checks the bread. Then she adds water and the potatoes. When the water begins to boil, they lower the heat and wait until the vegetables are soft. The beans go in near the end because they are already cooked.

Before the guests arrive, Mina uses a clean spoon to taste the food. The flavor is gentle, but she thinks it needs a little more pepper. Ravi suggests adding a small amount of spice first, because people can add more at the table. They agree not to pour in a large amount of spice all at once. Mina places a little salt in a separate bowl for anyone who wants it. The bread smells good, and the outside is brown. They do not bake a second loaf because one is enough for six small portions.

At six o'clock, the guests arrive. Mina and Ravi serve the vegetable dish with warm bread, and the cheese stays in its own dish. One guest asks how much sugar is in the vegetables. Ravi explains that the small amount of sugar was used in the bread, not in the vegetables. The guests sit together at a long table, where there is room for everyone to talk and pass the bread. After the meal, everyone helps wash the kitchen equipment and shares one idea for next time. The story is fictional, and people should adapt food choices to their own needs.
